title: Two parallel booking systems: the Schedule-tab manual confirm bypasses all slot validation and can double-book against candidate self-bookings
expected: One slot authority. A recruiter-confirmed slot is validated like a candidate-booked one: a real dated instant, checked against offered times and already-confirmed bookings (Marek's scored criterion: no double-book, no past date).
got: The candidate path is exemplary (offeredSlotFor re-derives the label, transactions collision-check on ISO slot_at, MAX_RESCHEDULES caps churn). The recruiter path is not: ScheduleTab's Confirm posts the picked 'Day HH:MM' string straight to approve_event, which stores ANY non-empty string verbatim as the slot (db/pipeline.ts:1303) — no date (which Tuesday?), no check against schedule_invites' bookedSlots(), no offered-times membership. The manual grid even offers 10 hourly slots/day (08:00-17:00) while self-scheduling offers 2 config-driven times/day — two disjoint slot vocabularies on the same tab. Nothing prevents confirming a wall-clock time a candidate already self-booked.
evidence: app/_lib/schedule-slots.ts:146-164 (the validation the manual path lacks)
scope_note: A backlog item exists (idea-b0c16e22 'validate confirmed slot against…'), so the gap is known — but not accepted in accepted-gaps.md, so it stays a finding.
l2_priority: Book Tue 14:00 via a candidate token, then confirm the same wall-clock slot from the manual grid for another candidate — verify nothing objects and inspect what dateless slot text lands in comms/events.
suggested_acceptance: A recruiter-side confirm resolves to a dated ISO instant validated by the same offeredSlotFor/bookedSlots authority as candidate bookings, and a clash is refused with a visible reason.

title: Bulk invite: no dry-run, and the per-invite delivery outcome the API returns is discarded — 'invited: N' can mean N minted, 0 delivered
expected: His cardinal rule: a bulk candidate-facing action shows a preview (who it touches, the rendered message) before firing, and afterwards an explicit per-recipient sent/not-sent breakdown (mint success ≠ delivery success — the single-invite drawer already distinguishes them).
got: PipelineTab.bulkInvite() fires immediately on click — no confirm gate (bulk reject IS confirm-gated at :478,486), no rendered-template preview. The bulk API isolates each entry and returns { entryId, ok, dispatched } per invite, but the UI reads only `ok` and reports a single 'invited: N' count — dispatch is best-effort, so every invite can mint fine while every delivery fails, and the UI still reports full success. Marek would re-verify the whole batch in the Outbox by hand, erasing the time saved.
evidence: app/features/sub_pipeline/CandidateDrawer.tsx:883-887 (the single-invite honesty the bulk path drops)
l2_priority: Run a bulk invite with the comms channel failing (or entries that dead-letter) and record exactly what the UI claims vs what the Outbox shows.
suggested_acceptance: Bulk invite shows a pre-send summary (N candidates, rendered invite) and a post-send breakdown separating minted-and-delivered from minted-but-undelivered, with the failures actionable.

title: A live scheduling token cannot be revoked or expired — and the drawer's 'Revoke links' reads as if it does exactly that
expected: An undo/recall path for a mis-sent candidate-facing invite (wrong candidate, link shared too widely): revoke the token so it stops booking. His criterion: no-way-back on a candidate-facing action is a major.
got: schedule-store.ts has no revoke/expire/cancel for invites (grep: zero matches); tokens live until the linked entry goes terminal ([token]/route.ts:139-144 bounds the blast radius but only via reject/decline — a nuclear option for a mere wrong-link mistake). Worse, the CandidateDrawer 'Revoke links' button is documented as 'pull every live link for this candidate' but calls /api/interview/revoke, which revokes only voice-interview sessions — the scheduling token stays bookable, while the recruiter believes it's dead.
evidence: app/_lib/schedule-store.ts (no revoke/expiry API exists — confirmed by search)
l2_priority: Mint an invite, click 'Revoke links', then open the schedule token as the candidate — confirm it still books (the mislabel made live).
suggested_acceptance: Either 'Revoke links' also voids open schedule invites (picker shows a friendly closed message), or a dedicated cancel exists on the invite lifecycle panel — and the button copy names exactly what it covers.

title: English slot label ('Tue 10 Mar · 10:00') interpolated verbatim into Czech candidate confirmation/reminder emails
expected: Every candidate-facing message under the bank's name reads as one language — a Czech email carries a Czech date ('út 10. 3. · 10:00').
got: slotLabel() mints the canonical label from English DOW/MON tables server-side; the UI re-localizes from the ISO instant (useSlotLabel), but emails interpolate the stored English label directly into the localized cs body — SchedulePicker's own comment confirms the English label 'stays … the stored canonical value for the recruiter feed + emails'. Hits every cs confirmation, reminder, and interviewer brief.
ceiling: Display-side localization is done (SCH4); only the persisted label in comm bodies remains English.
l2_priority: Book a slot for a cs-locale entry and read the actual Outbox confirmation body — confirm the mixed-language date renders as predicted.
suggested_acceptance: Comm templates format the slot from the ISO slotAt in the recipient's locale instead of interpolating the stored English label.

title: No invite-mint affordance on the Schedule tab — the journey's first step lives two tabs away in the Pipeline drawer
expected: Cognitive-walkthrough step 1: a coordinator wanting to 'send a self-scheduling invite' looks at the Schedule tab and finds the action there (or an explicit pointer).
got: ScheduleTab renders the lifecycle panel + the manual week grid + per-card actions, but no way to mint/send an invite; the affordance is the CandidateDrawer's 'Create scheduling link' (per candidate) and the Pipeline bulk bar. The lifecycle panel's 'awaiting' section even lists invites he can't have sent from this tab. The empty state links to Decisions, not to inviting.
l2_priority: Watch where a first-time coordinator looks for 'send invite' — measure the detour to the Pipeline drawer.
suggested_acceptance: The Schedule tab offers a path to mint/send a self-scheduling invite (button on pending cards or a pointer in the lifecycle panel/empty state).

title: Invite lifecycle panel fetches once per mount — bookings/flags landing while the tab is open never appear
expected: The monitoring surface he'd keep open reflects new bookings/attention flags without a manual reload (the tab's interview-status poll refreshes every 6 s by contrast).
got: InviteLifecyclePanel loads /api/schedule in a mount-only effect (no interval, no focus listener); the upcoming/past split is even pinned to loadedAt. The neighboring interview-status poll (ScheduleTab.tsx:127-143) shows the established pattern it lacks.
l2_priority: With the tab open, book a slot via token — confirm the agenda doesn't update until reload.
suggested_acceptance: The lifecycle panel refreshes on an interval or window focus, like the interview-status poll beside it.

title: Delivery is Outbox-simulated by default, and seeded entries' recipient is a display name — 'delivered' means a queued audit row, not a reached inbox
expected: The journey DoD ('delivered — an Outbox row, not a link pasted elsewhere') is met; Marek additionally needs the seam named so 'sent' is never overclaimed.
got: sendComm routes to a durable local Outbox (status 'queued' — explicitly terminal in dev) unless COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL configures a real relay with retry + dead-letter alerting. Recipient resolves to a real contact only for inbound applicants; recruiter/Match-sourced (seeded) entries resolve to the candidate's display name, which a real relay would dead-letter. The build names this seam itself (code comments + docs/COMMS_DELIVERY.md) — honesty worth keeping.
ceiling: Real candidate reach requires COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL plus a deliverable address; for the seeded ČS pipeline the invite 'delivery' is a queued Outbox row addressed to a human name — a dev inbox + audit log, not an email in a candidate's mailbox.
l2_priority: Confirm the Outbox row for a minted invite is inspectable (Channels tab) and its status label doesn't read as 'sent' when the channel is the local outbox.
suggested_acceptance: Outbox rows for schedule invites are visible with an honest status vocabulary (queued vs sent vs failed) matching docs/COMMS_DELIVERY.md.

title: Strength: candidate self-booking is server-authoritative end to end — validated slots, collision-safe transactions, bounded reschedules, terminal-entry guard
expected: Scheduling that can't double-book, book the past, or be spoofed by the token holder.
got: Only a slot the server would offer is bookable (structural validation to the exact canonical instant; label re-derived, client text ignored); confirm/reschedule run as synchronous SQLite transactions with slot_at as collision identity; reschedules capped at 3 with the old slot freed and the reminder cycle reset; a rejected/declined candidate's still-valid token can neither book nor move an interview.
ceiling: Collision authority is global and host-blind — per-interviewer availability / real calendar sync is the deferred Phase 2 (schedule-slots.ts:25-26); and the recruiter-side manual confirm sits entirely outside this authority (MAREK-ISP-1).
suggested_acceptance: Keep: any change to booking must go through offeredSlotFor + the store transactions.

title: Strength: honest delivery states everywhere on the single-invite path — dispatched flag, unsent warning, confirmationSent softening, short-notice wording
expected: 'Odešlo to? A komu?' answered explicitly at each hop.
got: Minting auto-dispatches and the drawer shows green sent / amber NOT sent from the dispatched flag; the candidate's booked card softens its promise when the confirmation email failed (confirmationSent:false) instead of lying; short-notice bookings drop the 'reminder coming' promise the system can't keep; a booked-but-pipeline-didn't-advance drift is flagged with its reason on the recruiter's attention panel rather than swallowed.
ceiling: The same honesty is missing from the BULK path (MAREK-ISP-2), and 'sent' still means the Outbox/relay handoff, not an opened email.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: every new dispatch surface must expose its sent/unsent outcome the way these do.

title: Strength: the busy-calendar dead-end is designed out on both sides — zero slots flags the recruiter and gives the candidate a defined outcome
expected: A candidate hitting a fully-booked horizon must not stall silently.
got: The server detects zero offerable slots on the read that surfaces it, idempotently flags the invite (logs once on the 0→1 transition), the recruiter sees a red attention row, and the candidate gets an explicit 'all times taken — nothing to do, we'll open more' card, covering both first booking and reschedule (the reschedule case used to fall through to an empty grid).
ceiling: Opening more times is still manual (KP_INTERVIEW_TIMES config / freeing slots); the flag tells the recruiter, it doesn't fix capacity.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: zero-slot handling stays server-side and idempotent.

title: Deterministic fallback prep is generic template filler that fails his senior bar — mitigated by honest disclosure and a one-click regenerate
expected: Questions a seasoned manager would actually ask for THIS role; anything generic ('walk me through a time you used X') fails his bar even if it technically worked.
got: When the LLM is unavailable (no key, billing degrade --no-llm), the pack is 4 near-identical skill-templated questions + focus areas copied from missing must-haves. The system is honest about it: any non-'llm' source renders the caution badge 'Template fallback' + an amber note + 'regenerate with AI', so the degraded plan can never impersonate a tailored one. Structural design of the REAL path is sound (grounded prompt, 6/8); its live prose quality is unverifiable at L1.
scope_note: Keyless run ⇒ fallback is the expected degraded mode per the journey file ('Keyless: prep questions fall to the deterministic template') — severity applies to the LLM path's unproven live quality, not to the disclosed fallback existing.
l2_priority: With a real key, generate prep for a seeded ČS candidate and assert the questions name candidate-specific facts (CV highlights, repo evidence, missing must-haves) — the single decider for Tomáš's adoption. Budget 30-130 s.
suggested_acceptance: A live-generated pack contains >=4 questions referencing this candidate's actual CV/JD specifics; the fallback badge appears only when the model was genuinely unavailable.

title: Prep prompt never receives prior-round evidence — the pack can re-ask what the voice screen or recruiter notes already answered
expected: A senior interviewer builds round 2 on round 1: probe what the screen left open, skip what it settled.
got: runInterviewPrep calls runAutomationTask(entryId, 'prep', '') — the notes argument is hardcoded empty — and reasoning_context carries only candidate+job+match(+github). No voice-screen scorecard, no screening rationale, no recruiter notes reach the prompt, though all exist in the DB and the scorecard task already demonstrates the --notes-file plumbing.
evidence: app/_lib/automation-run.ts:165-169 (the notes plumbing the prep task doesn't use)
l2_priority: Generate prep for an entry with a completed voice screen — check whether the questions duplicate what the screen's scorecard already rated.
suggested_acceptance: The prep prompt receives available prior-round evidence (voice-screen scorecard summary / recruiter note) and the pack visibly builds on it.

title: Early-career prep packs mix English six-phase script prose into an otherwise Czech plan
expected: His criterion: screens and reasoning in plain Czech; a cs-generated pack reads as one language.
got: PREP2 localizes the LLM questions and the deterministic scaffolding, but the six-phase STUDENT_SCRIPT topics/probes deliberately stay English ('the fixed pedagogical script the voice agent delivers, not free prose') — so a cs prep for a student candidate interleaves English phase prose with Czech goals/signals. Deliberate, but a branch manager prepping a junior teller reads a bilingual document.
ceiling: Localizing the script means forking the fixed pedagogical script the voice agent delivers — a consistency trade-off, not a one-line fix.
l2_priority: Generate a cs prep for an early-career entry and judge how the mixed pack actually reads to a Czech manager.
suggested_acceptance: Either the student-script prose localizes, or the pack labels the phases as the agent's fixed script so the language switch is explained.

title: The interviewer brief silently depends on a deliverable email in a free-text field — a bare name means Tomáš arrives unbriefed, the skip visible only in the event log
expected: If he's assigned to the round, the brief + calendar hold reach him — or the assigner is told loudly at assignment time that they won't.
got: dispatchInterviewerBrief emails the brief + inline .ics only when the free-text interviewer value parses to an address; a bare 'Tomáš Dvořák' records interviewer_brief_skipped and returns. The skip lands in the entry's event history, but the prep modal's interviewer field (placeholder-only, no validation hint) gives no signal at input time, and the schedule card shows the name as if ownership were fully wired.
l2_priority: Assign a name-only interviewer, book a slot as the candidate, and trace where (if anywhere) a recruiter would notice the brief never went.
suggested_acceptance: The interviewer field hints 'add an email to receive the brief' and/or a skipped brief surfaces on the schedule card, not only in the event log.

title: Strength: the prep prompt is genuinely grounded (6/8) — full CV, real JD must-haves, match evidence, repo evidence, archetype shaping, recruiter locale — with a cache that tracks its inputs
expected: Not 'good machinery fed thin context': the questions should be derived from THIS candidate against THIS role.
got: The full extracted profile is serialized into the prompt alongside the real job's must/nice-to-haves, matched/missing skills, optional GitHub evidence, early-career provenance fields, and the recruiter's language; profile+evidence are folded into the cache key so an edited CV can't serve stale prep. Early-career entries swap to the six-phase student script so the plan matches the interview that will actually happen.
ceiling: Still ungrounded: prior-round evidence (TOMAS-ISP-2) and org/process context (ČS norms, comp band) — 6/8, not 8/8.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: any prep-prompt change preserves profile+JD+match+evidence grounding and the serialize-once cache-key pattern.

title: Strength: human work is first-class — scorecard/notes/interviewer survive regeneration, the rubric is archetype-fair with BARS anchors, and a saved verdict visibly gates to Decisions
expected: His scored criteria: same dimensions for every candidate, override allowed, one clear action with unambiguous confirmation.
got: Regeneration re-merges humanScorecard/userProgress/interviewer onto the rebuilt artifact and the modal re-seeds without echo-saves; the rubric is single-sourced (interview-rubrics.json) across TS and Python with per-level behavioral anchors and role-family industry axes; saving a recommendation seals a human decision record and gates the entry to scorecard_review with an explicit 'moved to Decisions' notice — a human-led round is no longer invisible.
ceiling: The scorecard attaches only after a prep artifact exists (404 otherwise) — an ad-hoc interview with no generated prep has nowhere to record a rubric.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: the re-merge seam and the DEC1 gating disclosure are load-bearing for trust.

title: Strength: the run-of-show is a contract, not prose — 15-30 min band enforced, sparse packs padded to a real plan, header duration provably equals the last block's end
expected: A timed plan he can actually run between two meetings, never a 7-minute stub labelled as an interview.
got: Pure, unit-tested timing module: fixed intro/wrap, per-question minutes that tighten as questions grow, an open-discussion block absorbing slack up to the 15-min floor, question cap keeping the ceiling at 30; the checkable chronology + signals give him live coverage without breaking eye contact (coverage meter).
ceiling: The band is fixed at 15-30 min — a manager wanting a 45-60 min senior loop can't stretch the plan.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: run-of-show.test.ts stays the guard on the timing contract.
